# One box, many owners

[A distributed array begins with an agreement about who owns each value.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A temperature field may contain millions of values, but a rank needs to
store only its own part. The decomposition describes that ownership.
It does not itself move field values, calculate a derivative, or fill a
halo. Keeping those responsibilities distinct makes parallel code easier
to reason about.

This refactors example 02. Its original two-subdomain demonstration is now
driven by the actual communicator size, so changing the launch changes
the decomposition being demonstrated.

## What must a partition preserve?

The global index set is

$$
I=\{0,\ldots,15\}\times\{0,\ldots,7\}\times\{0,\ldots,3\}.
$$ {#eq-global}

Let $I_r$ be the owned box of rank $r$. A correct partition satisfies
$\bigcup_r I_r=I$ and $I_r\cap I_s=\varnothing$ for $r\ne s$.
In particular,

$$
\sum_r |I_r|=16\cdot8\cdot4=512.
$$ {#eq-count}

The count is necessary but insufficient: an overlap could conceal a
missing region. The numerical check therefore enumerates all the small
boxes and verifies the union and pairwise uniqueness as well.

## Describe ownership in C++

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="partition" dedent=4}
```

Every rank knows the same global domain and constructs the same partition.
`local_box` selects its own index box. The reduction checks @eq-count
without collecting a global field.

The rest of [model.cpp](model.cpp) gathers only six integers per rank to
write `results/decomposition.csv`. Each row contains a rank, the three
global lower indices, and the three local sizes. An upper index is
`lower + size - 1`: OpenPFC index boxes have inclusive bounds.

## Change the number of owners

From this directory with a provisioned SDK:

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

The input is an empty JSON object; the small domain is deliberately stated
in the source. Compare one, two, and four ranks. The shapes and number of
rows change, while the union remains the same 512 cells. Do not hard-code
the assumption that a particular rank always owns the left half.

Next, change the global shape from `{16,8,4}` to `{8,16,4}` and update the
source's independent count. Predict which local shapes will change. The
partitioning policy is a numerical/runtime choice; the physical problem
should not depend on it.

## Where this agreement ends

The example check launches one and two ranks and validates every owned
global index. It does not claim optimal communication volume, load balance
for arbitrary physics, or support for more ranks than meaningful cells.
FFT algorithms may redistribute values between a real-space inbox and a
Fourier-space outbox; the [FFT layout lesson](../../fourier/field-layout/index.qmd)
explains why those are separate ownership descriptions.

For exact API contracts see the
[decomposition header](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/decomposition/decomposition.hpp).
Continue with [indices and memory offsets](../index-boxes/index.qmd).
The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.

:::
